analysis.title: ETD Rates Watch: Post-Midterm Degrossing Gives Way to Selective Redeployment
key_insights: The desk's hindsight read is that equity price action over the last few weeks was market degrossing ahead of the midterms, as reflected in various street surveys. Equities rebounded from the lows on Wednesday and the E-mini Nasdaq made a 4.9% intraday move.
Investors selectively redeployed capital after the midterms. Data centre exposure was sold, with CoreWeave down 9.9%, and defence names were also hit hard.

In rates, there was renewed interest in the belly of the US curve. The oil decline drove significant Gilt and OAT outperformance. The desk can rationalise the Gilt move ahead of the BoE meeting but not the OAT move, since nothing has really changed.
The BoE is expected to raise rates by 25bp to 4% on Thursday. Markets appear to expect a dovish hike, based on continued put selling to fund upside in SONIA options.

The largest SONIA flow was paper paying 0.75 up to 1.25 for 16.8k SFIM7 call condors versus a put spread. The desk prefers a nearer-dated structure, the SFIF7 95.65/95.75/95.85/95.95 call condor, which was bought for 2k in 5k after the desk suggested it earlier at 1.5 offered.
Similar put-selling-to-fund-upside trades appeared in Euribor, with accounts positioning for the end of the ECB hiking cycle. Paper paid 1.25 for 8k ERF7 call spreads versus a put spread.
Eurex option flows have dropped off, alongside weaker interest in European fixed income futures. SOFR option activity is also slowing, and the larger flows on Wednesday leaned towards liquidations.

Long Bond (USZ6) open interest rose 2.07% on Wednesday, more than TUZ6 (+1.18%) and TYZ6 (+1.02%). The desk is unsure how much to read into it. The QRA held no surprises, with the phrase 'at least' removed from the auction guidance.

A large block steepener traded in the US on Wednesday, 44.7k TU versus 10.2k WN. The desk thinks it is too early to conclude that Trump's spending plans will be harder to push through and ease pressure on long-end yields.

The desk finds it difficult to be too bearish rates and links this to ongoing call buying, which continued in the London morning with 19k TYZ6 108 calls paying 16. If oil keeps weakening and data centre construction is curtailed, demand and inflation pressure would fall, and the market would be right to challenge current central bank pricing. The desk is sceptical oil keeps falling.

Maersk raised its full-year outlook for the second time in three months. CEO Clerc cited demand continuing unabated on electrification and AI investment out of Asia, with land-side constraints absorbing capacity. The desk asks what happens if AI infrastructure demand falters.

UK retailer Next reported slower sales growth. Full-price UK sales grew 2% in the 12 weeks to 31 October, down from 3.6% in the first half. The company blamed rising household bills and warmer September weather. Overall sales beat expectations on a 32.2% rise in online international sales.

The AFR reports RBA members privately rebuked Deputy Governor Hauser for signalling a likely hike before the meeting, arguing it undermined independence and pre-committed the RBA. Assistant Governor Hunter said on TV the RBA is 'not quite done'. Board members will reportedly be more careful in public.

Hauser said on Thursday that public trust in the RBA is under strain after a series of hikes over 18 months, and that 'gains tomorrow may require pain today'. He did not recognise the view that the board had been driven into a corner.
earnings_insights: Maersk raised its full-year financial outlook for the second time in three months (reported 5 Nov). No figures were given in this note.

Next: full-price UK sales grew 2% in the 12 weeks to 31 October (reported 5 Nov), down from 3.6% in the first half. Overall sales beat expectations, driven by a 32.2% increase in online international sales.
CoreWeave shares fell 9.9% on Wednesday, part of a broader sell-off in data centre exposure. No earnings figures were cited.

trade_ideas.description: Buy SFIF7 95.65/95.75/95.85/95.95 call condor in SONIA options as a nearer-dated upside play into the BoE meeting
trade_ideas.rationale: The desk prefers nearer-dated upside plays to the longer-dated SFIM7 structure, given expectations of a dovish BoE hike.

risk_factors: AI infrastructure demand could falter, which would undercut the demand cited by Maersk and the data centre construction impulse.
Oil may not keep weakening, which the desk is sceptical about. That would undercut the case for challenging current central bank pricing.
Further weakness in data centre exposure and defence names after the midterm redeployment.
Central bank communication risk: the RBA is under strain over public statements that appeared to pre-commit it to hiking.
vol_and_positioning: SONIA options: renewed put selling to fund upside, with paper paying 0.75 up to 1.25 for 16.8k SFIM7 95.40/95.50/95.95/96.05 call condors versus the 95.00/94.90 put spread.
SFIF7 95.65/95.75/95.85/95.95 call condor bought for 2k in 5k. The desk had suggested it earlier in the morning at 1.5 offered.
Euribor: paper paid 1.25 for 8k ERF7 96.9375/97.0625 call spreads versus the 96.75/96.50 put spread, playing for the end of the ECB hiking cycle.
Eurex option flows have dropped off and SOFR option activity is slowing, with the larger flows on Wednesday biased towards liquidations.
Open interest rose 2.07% in USZ6, 1.18% in TUZ6 and 1.02% in TYZ6 on Wednesday.
Block steepener in the US on Wednesday: 44.7k TU versus 10.2k WN.
Call buying in US Treasury futures continued into the London morning on Thursday, with paper paying 16 for 19k TYZ6 108 calls.

tension_points.bull_case: If oil keeps weakening and the data centre construction impulse is curtailed, demand and inflationary pressure fall, so the market is right to challenge current central bank pricing. Ongoing call buying in Treasury futures fits this.
tension_points.bear_case: The desk is sceptical oil keeps weakening. Maersk reports demand unabated on AI and electrification investment, and the inflationary impulse has been seen everywhere.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Oil stops weakening or the data centre construction impulse is not curtailed.
